messages.subject: GC-content window size vs. binning window size
messages.subject_clean: GC-content window size vs. binning window size
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Should "GC-content window size"  identical to "binning window size"?
50 bp window is suggested for both parameters in the vignette, but I would like to know if we can use different window sizes for the two parameters.

Thank you in advance,

Hoon

messages.subject: Re: GC-content window size vs. binning window size
messages.subject_clean: GC-content window size vs. binning window size
messages.body_plain:
Hi Hoon,

God point, sometime the documentation leave thing not covered in details.

You can experiment with different sizes of both, but the two are independent from each other.
I found 50 for the GC to be a good compromise. For the binning, in case of WGS, I usually increase the binning to 200 nt.

Best

Francesco

messages.subject: sequenza.extract error
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm new to sequenza and try to evaluate the tool.
Unfortunately I have troubles to use sequenza.extract on a windowed seqz file. The error is:

test2 <- sequenza.extract("xxxxxx_small.seqz.gz")
Processing chr1: Error in scan(file = file, what = what, sep = sep, quote = quote, dec = dec,  :
 scan() expected 'an integer', got '15.3921568627'

the first lines in xxxxxx_small.seqz.gz are:

chromosome      position        base.ref        depth.normal    depth.tumor     depth.ratio     Af      Bf      zygosity.normal GC.percent      good.reads      AB.normal       AB.tumor        tumor strand
chr1    12928   N       15.3921568627   17.0    1.084   1.0     0       hom     63      51      N       .       0
chr1    12947   C       13      14      1.077   0.929   0       hom     63      14      C       A0.071  A1.0

xxxxxx_small.seqz.gz was created using

sequenza-utils bam2seqz [...] --chromosome chr1 > xxxxxx
sequenza-utils seqz_binning -w 50 -s xxxxxx | pigz -p 12 > xxxxxx_small.seqz.gz

Is there anything I'm doing wrong?
I'm using sequenza-utils downloaded from git on May 5th 2017.

I should note that I had to apply the following change to wig.py in order to be able to run bam2seqz:

--- wig.py      2017-04-27 10:48:48.000000000 +0200
+++ /usr/local/bioinf/python/python-2.7.13/lib/python2.7/site-packages/sequenza_utils-2.2.0-py2.7-linux-x86_64.egg/sequenza/wig.py      2017-05-08 10:12:12.000000000 +0200
@@ -27,7 +27,7 @@
            self._end = self._start + self._span
            return ((self._chromosome, self._start, self._end), (self._val,))
        except ValueError:
-            line, chrom, span = wig_line.strip().split()
+            line, chrom, span = wig_line.strip().split(None, 2)
            self._chromosome = chrom.split('chrom=')[1]
            self._span = int(span.split('span=')[1])
            pos, self._val = next(self._wig).strip().split('\t', 1)

It seems that the wig header line created from my bams has more than 3 fields.

Thanks
  Dietmar

messages.subject: Re: sequenza.extract error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dietmar,

I don’t think you are doing anything wrong, it seems a bug in the new binning function.
The average depth normal and tumor should be rounded to integers, otherwise the R package will get the error you encountered.

Can you try to modify here: https://bitbucket.org/sequenza_tools/sequenza-utils/src/1a7736cf4bfbc02937ceecdc9598d7d990b2bd43/sequenza/seqz.py?at=master&fileviewer=file-view-default#seqz.py-311
with something like:

avg_line = [self._last_chromosome, self._last_position, 'N', int(round(self._n_depth / self._n, 0)),
                    int(round(self._t_depth / self._n, 0)), round(self._ratio / self._n, 3),
                    1.0, 0, 'hom’, gc, self._n, 'N', '.', '0']

I’ve push the changes in the git repo if you don’t want to modify it yourself (I haven’t changed the wig.py code yet, so you could merge your branch or just copy the seqz.py file….).

Thanks a lot for reporting the issue and I’ll look closely into the wig issue as well: did you use a GC wig downloaded from UCSC? I might just take your fix for now.

Thanks again

Francesco

Hi Francesco,

thanks for your answer. I'll try your fix.

Regarding the GC wig:
I created it on my own. The first line look like this:

variableStep chrom=chr1 AC:CM000663.2 gi:568336023 LN:248956422 rl:Chromosome M5:6aef897c3d6ff0c78aff06ac189178dd AS:GRCh38 span=50

The command was:
sequenza-utils GC-windows -w 50 GRCh38.d1.vd1/GRCh38.d1.vd1.fa | pigz -p 8 > GRCh38.d1.vd1.gc50Base.txt.gz

I guess the GC-windows util is using the entire fasta header lines, which in my case is:

>chr1  AC:CM000663.2  gi:568336023  LN:248956422  rl:Chromosome  M5:6aef897c3d6ff0c78aff06ac189178dd  AS:GRCh38

HTH
  Dietmar

messages.subject: suggest about selecting normal loci based on normal cnv
messages.subject_clean: suggest about selecting normal loci based on normal cnv
messages.body_plain:
Dear Francesco,

I used sequenza on my species' data, which genome has massive complex SVs. The recommended ploidy of some samples range from 4 to 6, but it should be 2 according to the karyotype FISH analysis. And the CNV profile also become doubled following the tetraploid or hexaploid estimation. I also tried by adjusting some parameters, but there wasn't any big changes.
I think your grid-based max bayes inferring model is absolutely reasonable, except the assumption of the constat normal ploidy. From paper nature19823, I get enlighten that they call CNV on normal sample, then exclude the loci in INDEL region in normal sample before estimating ploidy and cellularity. From my knowledge, sequenza will be unbiased if the normal ploidy changes are considered.
Expect your opinion and updates :)

Best!
Xuan

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've been following the instructions in the sequenza usage example (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sequenza/vignettes/sequenza.pdf), and at the moment my analysis keeps failing at "3.3 Generate a seqz file".
I'm able to generate the GC content file, and convert my bam file to pileup format, but once I attempt to generate the seqz file it runs for a while (sometimes up to half an hour, sometimes less than 5 minutes) before stopping and producing the error: "Something went wrong on the block counting!!"

When looking at the output files, they all stop at different points on chromosome 1, and some of the fields seem incomplete, eg: the last ten lines of one example:
chr1    42816708        G       12      12      1.0     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      G       .       0

chr1    42816713        C       9       13      1.444   1.0     0       hom     66.0    13      C       .       0
chr1    42816714        T       9       12      1.333   1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      T       .       0
chr1    42816715        G       8       13      1.625   1.0     0       hom     66.0    13      G       .       0
chr1    42816716        G       8       12      1.5     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      G       .       0
chr1    42816717        A       8       12      1.5     1.0     0       hom     66.0    12      A       .       0

When generating the pileups I output huge numbers of errors with some variation of: "[fai_fetch_seq] The sequence "chrEBV" not found", although when I look at the output the pileups themselves appear fine.
Could there be an issue with the pileups when is affected the seqz conversion?

And advice you could give would be very much appreciated.
Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: suggest about selecting normal loci based on normal cnv
messages.subject_clean: suggest about selecting normal loci based on normal cnv
messages.body_plain:
Dear Xuan,

Thanks for your input. |I actually think assessing the normal-only cnv state is a lacking point in the current pipeline.
I’m working on a new version that treats normal and tumor separately (we solved a memory issue that was preventing it before).
That at least would give the possibility of visual inspection if the CNV are present in the normal.

The preprocessing step,in its current state, is ditching completely the indels calls (either somatic or germlines), We could in principle test if they can be taken into account to discard or give less a given region…
We could make additional check in the pipeline to deselective/penalise genomic regions with germline indels/cna
In practice is not so easy to systematically model - principally due to the variance expected from sample to sample (not patients, just sequencing data in general), and the various bias may have different causes.

Thanks again for your valuable input, I hope to have more update on the topic soon

Best

Francesco
